result.reportText:
# Climb batch 35, rung A: an exit out of an atomic block keeps the block's writes, on both paths (row 1039)

- problem: an exit out of an `atomic` block to an enclosing `label` lost the block's writes on both paths, as the batch's probes measured on the base: `explorations/compile-ladder/plan-35/probes/fixes-35.md:19` (walk) and `:43` (compiled); ledger row 1039.
- spec: `Specification/basic/expressions/atomic.tex:59-63`, section "Atomic Expressions": "If it completes abruptly by exiting to an enclosing \KWD{label} expression, writes within the block are retained and become visible to other threads."
- precedent: the commit at a normal end of the same block, on each path: `BaseTask.endTransaction` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/runtimeSystem/BaseTask.java:210-221`) and the commit in `FortressTaskRunner.doItOnce` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/evaluator/tasks/FortressTaskRunner.java:125-131`); and the shape of `leaveTransaction`'s own branch for `TXLeave`, whose stale abort takes the abort path (`BaseTask.java:310-316`).
- deviation: none from the specification. From the precedent: the compiled exit's commit runs in the block's handler, after the task's transaction is set back to the parent (`BaseTask.java:302`), where `endTransaction` sets it after the commit; the commit uses only the transaction object, so the order changes nothing it does.
- historical: `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/runtimeSystem/BaseTask.java` and `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/evaluator/tasks/FortressTaskRunner.java`, both files of the original 2012 tree (`BaseTask.leaveTransaction` itself is the revival's, `594da41299`; `doItOnce` is the team's).

One launch of the worker role worked this rung: the worktree did not exist when it started.

## What changed and why

Commits on `wip/rung-exit-out-of-atomic`: `eb2f652487` (the tests and the fix), `8bd7cfcf0a` (the expected failure of a sibling defect, NEW-A-1), and the commit that adds this report and `record.md`.

- Compiled (`BaseTask.leaveTransaction`, `BaseTask.java:284-323`). Every compiled `atomic` block's handler takes every throwable of its body or its commit and calls `leaveTransaction` (`CodeGen.forAtomicBlock`, `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java:2067-2100`, unchanged). An exit is a thrown `LabelExit` (F-373). `leaveTransaction` now commits the block's transaction when what leaves is a `LabelExit` (`BaseTask.java:303-309`): `transaction.TXCommit()` and `ftr.recordEndTransaction()`, the two calls of `endTransaction`. A commit that fails throws `TransactionAbortException`, which the branch takes as `t`, and the existing abort code then runs the block again where the abort names this transaction, or throws it on to the block of the ancestor that it names (`BaseTask.java:317-322`), as at a normal end, where the commit's abort reaches the same handler. Any other exception still goes through `TXLeave` and discards the writes (`:310-316`). The exit is thrown on after a commit that succeeds, so the label's handler takes it as before. A nested block's commit hands its reads and writes to its parent (`Transaction.TXCommit`, `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/runtimeSystem/Transaction.java:302-307`), so an exit that leaves a nested block and its outer one commits the inner into the outer, then the outer.
- Walk (`FortressTaskRunner.doItOnce`, `FortressTaskRunner.java:122-148`). Walk runs an atomic block in `doItOnce`, which committed only after a normal end and gave the transaction up uncommitted in its `finally`, so the cells kept the block's writes under a transaction that stayed active and was then aborted by the next reader (`interpreter/env/ReferenceCell.java`, `getValue`). A `catch (LabelException exit)` now commits as the normal end does and throws the exit on (`:133-141`); a commit that fails aborts the transaction and throws `AbortedException`, so that `doIt` runs the block again, as at a normal end. `NamedLabelException`, walk's exit with a target, extends `LabelException`. `forAtomicExpr` and `forTryAtomicExpr` both run `doItOnce` (`interpreter/evaluator/Evaluator.java:189`, `:216`).

The code generator is unchanged, so no compiled jar changes; the edit is in the runtime, which every compiled program loads.

## The tests: failing on the base, passing after

The two expected failures were promoted before the edit: `ProjectFortress/tests/XXXExitOutOfAtomicWalk.fss` became `tests/ExitOutOfAtomicWalk.fss`, and `compiler_tests/XXXExitOutOfAtomicCompiled.{fss,test}` became `compiler_tests/ExitOutOfAtomicCompiled.{fss,test}` (`tests=ExitOutOfAtomicCompiled`, `link`, `run`, `run_out_contains=PASS`); `ExitOutOfAtomicCompiledLink.test` takes the new name. Each test holds three cases: the single exit (`g := 7`), an exit that leaves a nested block and its outer one (`h := 1` in the outer, `k := 2` in the inner, both asserted), and 1000 iterations of a parallel `for`, each an exit out of an atomic block that increments one counter (`count`, asserted 1000).

The failing runs, on the base's code, in the worktree before the edit was first built (`git status` showed no change under `ProjectFortress/src`):

As written, the old code fails both tests at the single case, as above; with the other assertions removed for the run:

What a failed commit does, measured: the compiled test run five times at four threads with `FORTRESS_THREAD_STATISTICS=y` (`FORTRESS_THREAD_STATISTICS=y FORTRESS_THREADS=4 bin/fortress run ExitOutOfAtomicCompiled`, from `ProjectFortress/`):

So the contended exits abort and run again 93 to 291 times a run, and every one of the 1000 writes is kept once. The tally counts retries only at `recordEndTransaction`, which the exit's commit now calls. In this program the body reads `count` and writes it, then exits, so an abort comes at the read's validation or at the exit's commit (`Transaction.handOver`, whose global lock fails when another block committed after the snapshot, and whose validation then finds the read stale).

## Row 1041, run once after the fix

Its behaviour stays on both paths. `ONE_JVM=1 explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-N/merged-tests/junit.sh row1041 ProjectFortress/compiler_tests ExitAfterLabelCompletedCompiled.test`, on `eb2f652487`:

    OK (2 tests)

One consequence reaches the row's question: such an exit, run inside an atomic block, now commits that block's writes too, since neither path can tell an exit to an enclosing label from one to a label block that has completed. The program, under walk (old code through `old-fortress.sh`, new code through the worktree's `bin/fortress`, each at `FORTRESS_THREADS=1`):

    var kept: () -> () = fn (): () => ()
    var w: ZZ32 = 0
    make(): () = label gone
        kept := fn (): () => exit gone
      end gone
    run(): () = do
      make()
      try
        atomic do
          w := 5
          kept()
        end
      catch e
        LabelException => println("caught LabelException")
      end
      println("w = " w)
    end

    == ExitAfterLabelThroughAtomicProbe, old code (base), walk, one thread
    caught LabelException
    w = 0
    == ExitAfterLabelThroughAtomicProbe, new code, walk, one thread
    caught LabelException
    w = 5

Compiled, by reading: `leaveTransaction` commits for every `LabelExit`, and the exit then ends the program, as row 1041 says. This goes to the curator with item 562 (forCurator).

## Where the fix belongs, and the precedent search

The feature table's row for `atomic` names `runtimeSystem/BaseTask.java` for the compiled transactions and `Evaluator.forAtomicExpr` with `evaluator/transactions/` for walk (`explorations/coordinator/map/spec-to-implementation.md:176`); the map's B.11 says the compiled transactions live in `BaseTask`'s static methods that generated code calls, and that walk's tasks and transactions are a second, independent implementation (`explorations/coordinator/map/modules-and-phases.md:421-439`). The section names the same two places.

<!-- Climb batch 35, rung O: the modifier override on the compiled path. The code generator compiles it, by the checker's own table of what an override keeps from being inherited, and the checker refuses an override that overrides nothing (rows 650 and 653). -->
# Rung O: the modifier `override` compiled, and the checker's refusal of one that overrides nothing

- problem: rows 650 and 653 measured on the base, and the second wall once the modifier was let through: `explorations/compile-ladder/plan-35/probes/fixes-35.md:41-42`, `:50-57`
- spec: `Specification/basic/traits.tex:673-683` (section "Method Declarations", the modifier `override` and its static error)
- precedent: the code generator's own narrowing forwarder, a method at the inherited declaration's signature that forwards to the type's narrower one (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java:1675`, `dumpOverloadedMethodChaining`); the checker's check of an overriding return type, which reads the same table (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/typechecker/OverloadingChecker.scala:421-423`); walk's refusal and its words (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/evaluator/values/Constructor.java:677-701`)
- deviation: the class of a type holds, for each declaration that its own override hides, a method at that declaration's JVM signature that runs the override (a bridge), and no method that runs the hidden declaration: `CodeGen.java:1476-1480`, `:1224-1237`
- deviation: two forms stay code-generator walls with messages of their own, an override of or by a method with static parameters of its own, and one in a generic trait or object whose parameter types name a static parameter (row NEW-O-1): `CodeGen.java:1204-1213`
- deviation: the checker's message names the declaration by its arrow type and span, as its other messages do, where walk prints the unparsed header: `OverloadingChecker.scala:785-787`
- deviation: the typecheck test of row 653 has the `XXX` prefix, since a compiled test without it is red on any refusal (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/tests/unit_tests/FileTests.java:383-386`, `:419`): `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/XXXOverrideNothingCompiled.test:1`
- historical: `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java:3458-3461`, `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/typechecker/OverloadingChecker.scala:410-424`, `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/useful/STypesUtil.scala:1787-1812`, `Specification/appendices/changes.tex:6422`

One launch worked this rung: the worktree did not exist at its start, and the branch had no commit past the base.

## What changed and why

**The code generator (fork O1).** `fnDeclCompilableModifiers` holds `Modifiers.Override` (`CodeGen.java:3458-3461`), so `forFnDecl` no longer refuses the modifier. With that alone the object's class held the override and a second method of its JVM name for the pair with the hidden declaration, and failed to load (PRB section 3). The code generator now reads what an override keeps from being inherited from the checker's own table: `STypesUtil.overriddenNotProvided` (`STypesUtil.scala:1787-1812`) calls `providedAndOverridden` (`:1698`) over `allMethods`, with `paramsWithoutSelfApart` as the reading of parameter types, the reading that `allMethodsNotReplaced` already uses, and gives each declaration p that an override o keeps a type of the walk from inheriting and that the type does not provide, with o. Where no gathered declaration has the modifier it returns at once, so a type without an override (every type of both libraries) costs one pass over its gathered declarations.

- `dumpOverloadedMethodChaining` (`CodeGen.java:1353-1354`, `:1476-1480`): a hidden p is no overload of its name. Where o is the type's own, p is treated as a narrowing to o: a method at p's signature forwards to o (the precedent's `generateForwardingFor(..., true)`), and no dispatch method of the name is written. Where o is a supertrait's, p is skipped.
- `dumpMethodChaining` (`CodeGen.java:1097-1099`, `:1115`, `:1165`): a hidden p gets no forwarder to its trait's body; `overrideBridges` (`:1224-1237`) writes the bridge from p's signature to o where o is a supertrait's that the class does not reach through its first supertrait (an object `extends { X, W }` with `W`'s override), once for each p.
- `checkOverrideCompilable` (`:1204-1213`) stops two forms that the bridge cannot serve yet (row NEW-O-1): a generic method compiles to a closure finder, which a bridge does not reach; and at an instance of a generic trait or object that makes p's and o's parameter types equal, as `G[\Any\]` for `override f(x: Any)` over `A[\T\]`'s `f(x: T)`, the instance class held both under one signature, 'ClassFormatError: Duplicate method name "f" with signature "(Lfortress.AnyType$Any;)..."' (a probe before the wall).

The methods of the promoted test's object class, on the final code (`javap -p -c 'OverrideModifierCodeGeneration$B.class'` after `bin/fortress compile compiler_tests/OverrideModifierCodeGeneration.fss`):

    public fortress.CompilerBuiltin$String g(com.sun.fortress.compiler.runtimeValues.FZZ32);
         2: invokevirtual #14                 // Method g:(Lfortress/CompilerBuiltin$Number;)Lfortress/CompilerBuiltin$String;
    public fortress.CompilerBuiltin$String f?0(com.sun.fortress.compiler.runtimeValues.FZZ32);
         2: invokevirtual #17                 // Method "f?0":(Lfortress/CompilerBuiltin$Number;)Lfortress/CompilerBuiltin$String;
    public fortress.CompilerBuiltin$String f?0(fortress.CompilerBuiltin$Number);
    public fortress.CompilerBuiltin$String f?0?(fortress.CompilerBuiltin$Number);    (body: "f PASS")
    public fortress.CompilerBuiltin$String g(fortress.CompilerBuiltin$Number);
    public fortress.CompilerBuiltin$String g?(fortress.CompilerBuiltin$Number);      (body: "g PASS")

`f?0?` and `g?` are the bodies, and `f?0(Number)` and `g(Number)` the plain-named entries, as for any object method (a plain `object B extends A` that redeclares `f` and `g` at `ZZ32` gets the same pair). The two methods at `FZZ32` are the bridges at `A`'s signatures. The bridge is what makes the promoted test pass: the checker resolves `f(B, 17)` to the wrapper of `A`'s `f(A, FZZ32)`, which calls the interface method `A.f?0(FZZ32)`, and `B.g(17)` to `B.g(FZZ32)`, the numerals taking `A`'s declaration at their default type (row 694's territory). The run with the verifier on prints both lines: `bin/fortress run OverrideModifierCodeGeneration` gives `f PASS` and `g PASS` (verification is HotSpot's default for the class loader's classes; `bin/run` passes no flag that turns it off).

**The checker (fork O2).** `checkOverridesSomething` (`OverloadingChecker.scala:763-789`), called for each trait and object beside the return-type check of the same table (`:424`), refuses each declaration with the modifier that the type declares and that appears in no pair of `providedAndOverridden` as an override (`equal` false): it overrides no inherited declaration of its name and kind, with self at the same position, whose parameter types without self are strictly below its own. Equal parameter types override nothing (review-queue item 73's default, "strict"). A declaration whose parameter types, or those of an inherited one of its name and kind, have a missing type is not judged, since that type has its own error. The message, with walk's words:

    Invalid override of f in object B:
        (B, String)->String @ .../XXXOverrideNothingCompiled.fss:9:3-37 has the modifier override and does not override any inherited declaration.

**The specification.** Appendix I's entry "The features not yet supported, in the preface and the introduction" (`\seclabel{revival-supported}`) no longer names the code generator's refusal of `override` in its effect (`Specification/appendices/changes.tex:6422`).

## The runs

The tests first, on the base's code, before the first build of the edit (the build started after 10:03 UTC):

    $ echo "Expected failure: OverrideModifierCodeGenerationLink red, CompilerError ... Don't know how to compile this kind of FnDecl. node = f(self:B,other:Number):String; ..."
    $ ONE_JVM=1 explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-N/merged-tests/junit.sh base ProjectFortress/compiler_tests OverrideModifierCodeGenerationLink.test OverrideModifierCodeGeneration.test OverrideNothingCompiled.test    (10:02:51Z)
    . link ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/OverrideModifierCodeGeneration
     UNEXPECTED exception
        Don't know how to compile this kind of FnDecl. node = f(self:B,other:Number):String
    3) ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/OverrideNothingCompiled(...)AssertionFailedError: Must satisfy typecheck_err_contains; expected
    Tests run: 4,  Failures: 4,  Errors: 0

After the fix, `OverrideNothingCompiled` was red for its plain name: a compiled test without the `XXX` prefix fails on any non-zero exit ('Must satisfy FAIL or fail should not appear in output typecheck'), so a refusal test is named `XXX`, as `XXXOverrideReturnTypeNotSubtype` is. Renamed `XXXOverrideNothingCompiled`, it was run on the old code (`old-fortress.sh`), first with an expectation that named the wrong message ('Missing expected failure'; the harness checks the key first), then again:

    $ echo "Expected failure: on the base's code, XXXOverrideNothingCompiled red, 'Saw wrong failure': its typecheck_err_contains key is unmet, ..."
    $ explorations/coordinator/tools/old-fortress.sh /home/user/fortress-base42 .../tmp/old-caches junit .../compiler_tests/XXXOverrideNothingCompiled.test    (10:10:05Z)
     Saw failure, but did not satisfy typecheck_err_contains; expected
    does not override any inherited declaration
    1) .../XXXOverrideNothingCompiled(...)AssertionFailedError: Saw wrong failure. typecheck

The first `XXX` test, shown red on a deliberate change: its override widened to `Any`, so that it overrides `A`'s `f`, the checker accepts the program, and `junit.sh red ... XXXOverrideNothingCompiled.test` printed 'Saw wrong failure. typecheck'; restored, it reads 'Saw expected failure'.

The tests written after the first fix, on the old code: `OverrideBridgesCompiledLink` and `OverrideBridgesCompiled` red at the link ('Don't know how to compile this kind of FnDecl. node = f(self:B,other:Number):String', 10:25:15Z); `XXXOverrideOverStaticParameterCompiled` and `XXXOverrideGenericMethodCompiled` red, 'Did not satisfy compile_exception_contains' (the base's message is the FnDecl refusal, 10:22:37Z); `XXXOverrideConditionalExtensionChecker` green on the base, 'Saw expected failure' (row NEW-O-2 was there before this rung).

The passing run, after the last change of code (`c5c2bd6d7a`, the tree's code at 10:25):

    $ ONE_JVM=1 explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-N/merged-tests/junit.sh fix3 ProjectFortress/compiler_tests <the 7 new tests and the 12 compiled tests that write override or test it>
    . run ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/OverrideModifierCodeGeneration (288ms) f PASS
    . run ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/OverrideBridgesCompiled (288ms) PASS
    OK (26 tests)

`OverrideBridgesCompiled` then took a case more, a generic object's override called through its trait's type (`07617087a6`, a test edit only): on the old code it is red at the link as before ('Don't know how to compile this kind of FnDecl', 'Tests run: 3,  Failures: 3', 10:45Z), and on `c5c2bd6d7a`'s code `junit.sh fix4 ... OverrideBridgesCompiledLink.test OverrideBridgesCompiled.test` prints '. run ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/OverrideBridgesCompiled (623ms) PASS' and 'OK (3 tests)' (10:44:46Z).

`ant testQuick` once on `c5c2bd6d7a`, after the last edit of code (before that test edit): 'BUILD SUCCESSFUL', 'Total time: 8 minutes 39 seconds'; `CompilerJUTest` 'Tests run: 1794, Failures: 0, Errors: 0', `OtherCompilerJUTest` 263, `LibraryJUTest` 86, each with 0 failures (climb batch 34b's gate: 1785, 263, 86; the 9 more are this rung's new commands).

## Where the fix belongs, and the precedent search

The map gives the place: the modifier's refusal is in `forFnDecl`, and an object's inherited methods are gathered in `dumpMethodChaining` and `dumpOverloadedMethodChaining` (the brief's `:1096` and `:1287`). The rung's fork O1 names the source of the hiding, the checker's table, not a second reading of the rule; `allMethodsNotReplaced` (`STypesUtil.scala:1762`) is the precedent for a code-generator view of that table, and the narrowing forwarder (`CodeGen.java:1675`) for a method at an inherited signature that runs the type's own declaration. The checker's refusal sits beside the return-type check of the same pairs (`OverloadingChecker.scala:421-423`). No earlier rung repaired an `override` in the code generator; the one precedent of a bridge in a class for another declaration's signature is the narrowing branch, one site in `CodeGen.java` (`:1675`), with its generic variant beside it.

## What the specification settles

The traits chapter states the rule: an `override` overrides each inherited declaration whose parameter type without self is a strict subtype of its own, and it is a static error if it overrides none (`Specification/basic/traits.tex:673-683`). A type inherits no overridden declaration (`:584-590`). It settles every form tested here; the forms that stay walls (NEW-O-1) and the checker's refusal under a conditional extension (NEW-O-2) are departures from it, each with its `XXX` test.

## Old against new

- Walk's override programs under `fortress typecheck` (the compiler's prelude), copied from `tests/`, old and new: refused now with the new message alone, where the base accepted them: `OverrideNothingWalk`, `OverrideEqualTypesWalk`, `OverrideNothingInTraitWalk`, `OverrideNothingGenericWalk`, `OverrideNothingGenericTraitWalk` (walk refuses each at load). Accepted on both: `OverrideInTraitWalk`, `OverrideGenericInstanceEqualTypesWalk`, `OverrideObjectExpressionWhereBoundWalk`, `disp0`, `disp1`, `FunctionalMethodMeetProvided`. Refused on the base by the overloading check and now also by the override check: `OverrideAfterWhereBoundWalk` (walk refuses it), `OverrideConditionalExtensionWalk` (walk runs it; row NEW-O-2), `XXXOverrideNothingConditionalExtensionWalk` (walk loads it; row 693). Refused by a call's error, on both, before any override check: `OverrideNothingGenericObjectExpressionWalk`, `XXXOverrideObjectExpressionOverParamWalk`; an object expression's override is not checked (row NEW-O-3).
- Compiled and run, new only (the base refuses every override): `disp0` prints `f PASS`, `g PASS`; `OverrideInTraitWalk` prints `PASS`; `disp1` and `OverrideGenericInstanceEqualTypesWalk` stop at the new wall.
- Row 694's form after the fix, `B.f(3, 4)` with `B`'s `override f(x: Number, y: NN32): String` over `A`'s `f(x: NN32, y: NN32): Any`, `bin/fortress typecheck` on `c5c2bd6d7a`, rc=255, unchanged: 'Ambiguous coercion in method invocation B.f: of the declarations applicable to an argument of type (NaturalNumeral[\1,10,3\], NaturalNumeral[\1,10,4\]) only by coercion, none is more specific than every other: (NN32, NN32)->Any; (Number, NN32)->String.' Walk prints `B`. The row stays open.

## The stages, and the checker's time (P-148)

The machine: nproc 4, Intel Xeon @ 2.30GHz, OpenJDK 25.0.4.1, `FORTRESS_THREADS=1`.

- The count stage, timed. Base, on the base build (`295c215c2c`, whose code is the base's: `git diff --stat 295c215c2c 13f4fdea75 -- ProjectFortress Library` prints nothing), load 0.24 at start: 'real 1m26.350s'. Change, on `c5c2bd6d7a`, load 1.16 at start: 'real 1m13.606s'. The two tables are equal (`diff` prints nothing), and equal to climb batch 34b's gate table (`#total 0`, `#locations 0`, `#crash none`); the two `run.txt` files are equal once each run's tree and scratch paths are replaced by one word.

No gain to take, so the pass changed no code, and no `pass` run or second `ant testQuick` was made; the change's results stand for it. The pass made before the timing: the check visits only declarations with the modifier, and the code generator's table returns at once for a type without one.
- The distance stage, on `c5c2bd6d7a`: `explorations/coordinator/tools/distance/compare.sh explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-34b/gate/distance.txt tmp/.../distance-postedit.txt` prints 'DISTANCE SAME   0'; the tables are equal but for `#seconds` and `#machine`; the per-site list (`dist-post/errors.tsv`) is equal to `explorations/compile-ladder/gate/distance-sites.tsv`, its header alone. ## Sentences of the specification made false

- problem: walk on the base fails both forms, 'FAIL: a ZZ32: 11449 =/= a ZZ32: 1075369; two indices, then a superscript' and 'FAIL: a ZZ32: 3 =/= a ZZ32: 1; the right side ran once' (`explorations/compile-ladder/plan-35/probes/fixes-35.md:17-18`)

- precedent: `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/evaluator/Evaluator.java:1034-1045` (`forSubscriptExpr` evaluates every index with `evalExprListParallel`); the desugarer's own rewriters `Local` and `Member` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/rewrite/DesugarerVisitor.java:93`, `:151`), chosen by the flag that `forFnDecl` reads (`DesugarerVisitor.java:792`)
- deviation: the subscript is repaired in `evalAndInvokeMethod`, the helper that `mathItemApplication` calls (`Evaluator.java:1069-1071`), not in `mathItemApplication` itself (`Evaluator.java:1167-1189`), which is unchanged; the tuple binding's repair reaches a field's tuple binding in an object and in an object expression too, beyond the top level that fork W2 names (`DesugarerVisitor.java:854`, `:872`)
- historical: `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/evaluator/Evaluator.java:1069-1071`; `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/rewrite/DesugarerVisitor.java:853-881` (both lines edited are the team's, at `a874948ac` `Evaluator.java:935` and `DesugarerVisitor.java:873`)

One launch worked this rung. Its commits on `wip/rung-walk-subscript-tuple-binding`, from the base `13f4fdea75`:

    2da0bd16c4 Walk: a subscript before a superscript or a subscript keeps its first index; a tuple binding's right side runs once (rows 1, 1026)
    73805235f1 SubscriptThenSuperscriptWalk: its row object named Lane, apart from the library component's Row
    7c7689ee6e SubscriptThenSuperscriptWalk: two subscripts then a superscript, and a subscript then a juxtaposed item

The code state is `2da0bd16c4`'s: the two later commits change only the test file. The base build `/home/user/fortress-base42` is at `295c215c2c`; `git diff --name-only 295c215c2c 13f4fdea75` lists no path under `ProjectFortress/` or `Library/` (only `.claude/`, `docs/` and `explorations/`), so the old code that ran from it is the base's code.

## What changed and why

1. **The subscript (row 1, fork W1).** A primary whose math items are a subscript and then a superscript, another subscript or an expression, as `m[3,7]^2`, `g[3][7]` or `x[5]k`, applies each item in turn to the element before it (`Evaluator.java:1191-1222`, `stepThree`). For a subscript, `mathItemApplication` calls `evalAndInvokeMethod(front, opString, sub.getExprs(), loc)` (`Evaluator.java:1187`). That helper evaluated its list by `evalInvocationArgs`, which evaluates "the tail of the list, EXCLUDING THE FIRST ELEMENT" (`Evaluator.java:1380-1397`): right for a juxtaposition's list, whose first element is the function, wrong for a subscript's indices. `evalAndInvokeMethod` now evaluates every index with `evalExprListParallel`, as `forSubscriptExpr` does (`Evaluator.java:1037`). Its one caller is `mathItemApplication`: `grep -rn "evalAndInvokeMethod" ProjectFortress/src` prints only `Evaluator.java:1069`, `:1070` and `:1187`. `evalInvocationArgs` is unchanged for its three other callers (`Evaluator.java:1312`, `:1356`, `:1377`), whose lists begin with the function.
2. **The tuple binding (row 1026, fork W2).** Walk's own rewrite, `DesugarerVisitor.forVarDecl`, turns `(first, second) = e` into a temporary `*tuple_<span> = e` and one declaration per name. Each name's initializer was a field reference on `e` itself, so `e` ran once for each name and once more (the temporary). Each name now reads its element from the temporary: `Expr tempRef = (isMember ? new Member() : new Local()).replacement(ExprFactory.makeVarRef(at, temp))` (`DesugarerVisitor.java:872`), where `isMember` is the flag `atTopLevelInsideTraitOrObject` read on entry (`:854`), before the method clears it. At the top level the reference is a variable at the top level's depth, as every top-level name's reference is; inside an object or an object expression it is `$self.*tuple_<span>`, as a reference to a sibling field is. The same member serves a field declared in tuple notation, which ran its right side three times on the base too (below); the objects chapter gives such a field the meaning of a top-level declaration (`objects.tex:295-297`).

Walk's desugarer is walk's alone: its only constructions are `interpreter/env/CUWrapper.java:215` and `:217`, and `explorations/coordinator/map/modules-and-phases.md:349` places it after the shared phase chain, with no counterpart in the compiler. So the compiled path is unchanged.

- `ProjectFortress/tests/SubscriptThenSuperscriptWalk.fss`, new, from the planner's program: `m[3,7]^2`, `m[7]^2`, `x[5]^2` for `x: ZZ32[7]`, `B.f()[5]^2` after a dotted call, `g[3][7]` and `g[3,7][2]` for a `Grid` whose subscript answers a `Lane` with a subscript of its own, `g[1][2]^2`, and `x[5]k`.

- `ProjectFortress/tests/FieldTupleBindingOnceWalk.fss`, new: a field's tuple binding in an object and in an object expression runs its right side once.

## Where the fix belongs, and the precedent

- Walk evaluates a math primary itself (`skill interpreter.md`, "Where a fix of walk belongs"; `Evaluator.java:1247-1280`, `forMathPrimary`), so the subscript is repaired in the evaluator. The tuple binding's defect is in walk's own rewrite, `DesugarerVisitor`, which the compiler does not run (`modules-and-phases.md:349`); it is repaired there.
- Walk applies a subscript at four sites: `Evaluator.forSubscriptExpr` (`Evaluator.java:1037`), `LHSToLValue.forSubscriptExpr` (`LHSToLValue.java:77`), `LHSEvaluator.forSubscriptExpr` (`LHSEvaluator.java:46`) and `mathItemApplication` (`Evaluator.java:1184-1188`). The first three evaluate every index (`x.getSubs()`); the fourth was the only one that dropped one. So the precedent, `forSubscriptExpr`, has no other site to repair: 0.
- The record's precedent for the binding is the compiled path's: the right side kept once in a hidden class, each name reading its element from it (F-369, `compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java:6908`). Walk's desugarer already made the temporary, with the team's comment "Introduce a temporary, then initialize elements piece-by-piece" (`DesugarerVisitor.java:859-860`), and never read it.
- The ways the language and the tree offer, for each fork, are under "Decisions".

## What the specification settles

- A subscript that is a math item: `juxtameaning.tex:146-168`. A math item may be a subscripting; the reassociation replaces the first non-expression element "and the element immediately preceding it (which must be an expression) with a single element that does the appropriate operator application". The application of a subscripting operator method passes the indices written (`Specification/advanced/subscripting.tex`, section "Subscripting Operator Method Declarations"). So `m[3,7]^2` is `(m[3,7])^2`, `g[3][7]` is `(g[3])[7]`, and `x[5]k` is `(x[5]) k`, as the compiled path gives (F-387).
- A tuple binding: `variables.tex:99-120` declares several variables together by tuple notation, for "a function application [that] returns a tuple of values"; the right side is one expression, whose one value the names take apart. A field: `objects.tex:295-297`, "syntactically identical to a top-level variable declaration ... with the same meanings", and "Field initialization occurs in textual program order: evaluation of each initial-value expression must complete before evaluation of the next" (`objects.tex:300-304`).

The full text is committed at explorations/compile-ladder/rung-self-not-first-dispatch/REPORT.md on wip/rung-self-not-first-dispatch (c89b2f356b); it is reproduced here word for word.

# Rung S: the dispatch method of a functional method whose self is not first

- problem: on the compiled path, where an object overloads an inherited functional method by declarations of its own whose self is not first, a call dies with `ClassCastException` (row 573) or answers the object's declaration for every argument (row 1038), measured by the planner on the base: explorations/compile-ladder/plan-35/probes/fixes-35.md:40
- spec: a functional method's parameter type holds self at its place, and a call runs the most specific declaration applicable to it at run time: Specification/basic/overloading.tex:175-181 and Specification/basic/overloading.tex:298-312
- precedent: the layout of a functional method's own locals, the receiver in local 0 and every parameter but self after it in order (`CodeGen.addParams`), which the dispatch method's descriptor already follows (`getSignature(selfIndex)`, OverloadSet.java:2565): ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java:3369
- deviation: none; the dispatch method of a dotted method, of a top-level function and of a functional method with self first keeps its bytecode (javap, section "Each program run old against new"): none
- historical: ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/OverloadSet.java: ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/OverloadSet.java:2504

One launch worked this rung. The worktree was seeded by the brief's command (exit 0, 3 s) from the base build `/home/user/fortress-base42` (at 295c215c2c, an ancestor of the base 13f4fdea75 with no difference under `ProjectFortress/` or `Library/`). Commits on `wip/rung-self-not-first-dispatch`, cut from 13f4fdea75: c03be68be8 (the three tests promoted, the self-second-of-three case), 630708ad6d (the trait case), 9d9a67df82 (the fix), and the commit of this report.

## What changed and why

The dispatch method of a functional method, in a trait's or an object's class, is an instance method of the receiver's class: self is the receiver, in local 0, and the other arguments follow in their order without self (its descriptor skips self, OverloadSet.java:2565; the forwarding wrapper pushes self as the receiver and then the others, CodeGen.java:3736-3780). `OverloadSet.generateCall` loaded the argument at place `j` of a member's parameters from local `j + offset` for its type test (OverloadSet.java:1538 on the base) and from local `j + firstArgIndex` for the arm's call (OverloadSet.java:1876 on the base), with `firstArg()` 0 for a functional method (OverloadSet.java:2491-2493). That is right only where self is first. With self second or last, the argument before self was read from the local before its own: the first argument from local 0, the receiver. So the type test tested the receiver, and the last arm, which has no test, cast the receiver to the argument's type: a `ClassCastException` where the receiver is not of that type (row 573), and the object's own declaration for every argument where it is (row 1038).

The edit adds `argumentLocal(j, first)`, the local of the argument at place `j`, `j + first` in `OverloadSet` (OverloadSet.java:2357-2363), overridden in `ForTraitOrObject` (OverloadSet.java:2495-2508): for a functional method, an argument before self's place is in the local after its place, `j + 1`, and one after self's place in the local at its place, `j + first` with `first` 0. The type test and the arm's call read it (OverloadSet.java:1538, :1876). For a dotted method (`selfIndex` is `NO_SELF`) and a top-level function the method gives what the two sites gave before. This is fork S1 of the batch (explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-35.md:449).

The three other sites of the file that read an argument's local are unchanged, each for its reason:

- the inference branch, `ALOAD j` (OverloadSet.java:1846), loads the parameters of a generic arm that `getFunctionToCall` converted to a function with self first, so its locals are at their places; for a functional method no program reaches it, since an object's generic functional method beside a plain one stops the code generator in `getFunctionToCall` (OverloadSet.java:2782, row 724);
- the varargs arm's array, `firstArgIndex + p + j` (OverloadSet.java:2031), takes the arguments after the `p` plain ones, self among them, so it is right wherever self stands among the plain parameters (read, not measured: the compiler's prelude refuses a varargs parameter);
- `generateLeafCall` (OverloadSet.java:1990) has no caller.

## The failing runs and the passing run

Before the first build of the edit, on the seeded base build's classes, the promoted tests through the harness (`junit.sh` with `ONE_JVM=1`, four threads; the machine: 4 CPUs, Intel Xeon @ 2.30 GHz, JDK 25.0.4.1). The first call echoed:

    # junit.sh s35base 2026-11-23T10:53:07Z; nproc 4; ... FORTRESS_THREADS=4; tree 13f4fdea75 with the next rung applied, not yet committed
    Caused by: java.lang.ClassCastException: class FunctionalMethodOverloadSelfLast$C cannot be cast to class FunctionalMethodOverloadSelfLast$N1 (...)
    Caused by: java.lang.ClassCastException: class FunctionalMethodCoverSelfSecond$Pq cannot be cast to class FunctionalMethodCoverSelfSecond$Ka (...)

`FunctionalMethodCoverSelfSecond`, `FunctionalMethodSelfSecondReceiverTested` and `FunctionalMethodMeetNarrowedSelfNotFirst` print `PASS` in the same run. The build before it: `ant compileAll`, 'BUILD SUCCESSFUL', then the library order, five compiles with exit 0.

## Where the fix belongs, and the precedent search

The map gives the compiled path's dispatch to `OverloadSet`, which emits one dispatch method per overloaded name (explorations/coordinator/map/modules-and-phases.md, "B.7 Overloading"). The rung's section names `ForTraitOrObject` and what `generateCall` emits for it. No earlier commit repaired an argument's local in `OverloadSet.java`: of the revival's commits to the file, only e9bc2ed3e3 (varargs) added a site that reads one, `armCallsVarargsDeclaration`, which is right wherever self stands. The file has five sites that read an argument's local (OverloadSet.java:1538, :1846, :1876, :1990-2018, :2031); the edit changes two, and section "What changed and why" gives the reason for each of the other three. The layout followed is the team's own: `CodeGen.addParams` (CodeGen.java:3369-3375) gives a functional method's body the receiver in local 0 and every parameter but self after it, and `functionalForwardingMethod` (CodeGen.java:3736-3780) calls the method so. `ForTraitOrObject` already holds the other facts of that layout, `loadThisForMethods`, `firstArg()` and `selfIndex()` (OverloadSet.java:2481-2493, :2510-2513), so the override sits beside them.

## What the specification settles

A functional method declaration with self at place `i` has the parameter type `Ps` with self at its `i`th element (Specification/basic/overloading.tex:175-181), and a call dispatches to the declaration applicable to it at run time that no other applicable one is more specific than (Specification/basic/overloading.tex:298-312), more specific by the subtype relation on the whole parameter types (:353-358). So each argument is tested at its own place, whatever self's place. Walk runs each call so; the compiled path now does too.

## Each program run old against new

Compiled with the old code (`explorations/coordinator/tools/old-fortress.sh /home/user/fortress-base42 tmp/.../old-caches compile P.fss`, then `run P`) and with the fix (`bin/fortress compile` and `run` with a private caches folder), on 9d9a67df82:

| program | old | new |
|---|---|---|
| `DispatchSelfFirstProbe` (self first, a probe in the rung's tmp) | `C1`, `C0` | `C1`, `C0` |
| `FunctionalMethodOverloadSelfLast` | `ClassCastException: ...$Do cannot be cast to ...$N1` | `PASS` |
| `FunctionalMethodCoverSelfSecond` | `ClassCastException: ...$Pq cannot be cast to ...$Ka` | `PASS` |
| `FunctionalMethodSelfSecondReceiverTested` | `FAIL:  3 =/= 1; mark(1, Pq): ...` | `PASS` |
| `FunctionalMethodMeetNarrowedSelfNotFirst` | `ClassCastException: ...$C cannot be cast to ...$N0` | `PASS` |

The dispatch methods, by `javap -c -p` of the jars (constant-pool numbers left out):

- self first, `DispatchSelfFirstProbe$C.pick?0(N1, S0)`: old and new identical; the type tests read `aload_1` (n) and `aload_2` (s), the arm's call `aload_0` (receiver), `aload_1`, `aload_2`.
- self second, `FunctionalMethodSelfSecondReceiverTested$Pq.mark?1(Any)`: old `aload_0; instanceof K` and `aload_0; checkcast` for x; new `aload_1; instanceof K` and `aload_1; checkcast`, the receiver `aload_0` only as the call's target. The same in each of `FunctionalMethodCoverSelfSecond$Pq`'s `mark?1(Any)`, `mark?1(Ka)` and `mark?1(Kb)`.
- self second of three, `FunctionalMethodMeetNarrowedSelfNotFirst$C.pick?1(N0, S1)`: old n at `aload_0`, s at `aload_2`; new n at `aload_1`, s at `aload_2`.
- self last, `FunctionalMethodOverloadSelfLast$C.pick?2(N1, S0)` and the trait's `FunctionalMethodOverloadSelfLast$D$DefaultTraitMethods.pick?2(N1, S0)` (its arms called by `invokeinterface`): old n at `aload_0`, s at `aload_1`; new n at `aload_1`, s at `aload_2`.

In the self-second-of-three class the order in which the dispatch methods are written, and so the constant pool's numbering, differs between the old and the new jar; the instructions of each method are the same up to those numbers.

## The stages, and the files for STAGE_BLIND

The brief has this rung run neither stage. The one source file edited is `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/OverloadSet.java`, the code generator's dispatch: `generateCall` is reached only from `generateBody` in the same class, and the class's dispatch writing only from the code generator (`CodeGen`, `CodeGenerationPhase`); the count stage and the distance stage run the checker, which does not reach it. `grep -rlw` over `ProjectFortress/tests`, `ProjectFortress/*_tests` and `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/` finds no other declaration of `FunctionalMethodOverloadSelfLast`, `FunctionalMethodCoverSelfSecond`, `FunctionalMethodSelfSecondReceiverTested` or `argumentLocal`.

## The sentences that the change makes false

- Specification: none. `grep -rn '~573\|~1038' Specification --include=*.tex` prints nothing, on the base and after; no `\revision`, `\note` or Appendix I effect speaks of the compiled dispatch of a functional method whose self is not first (`grep -rn -i "compiled path\|code generator" Specification --include=*.tex` with self, functional method or dispatch: one line, Specification/appendices/changes.tex:4461, on `self` returned at the instance's type, which the change leaves true).
- The skill, for the gather: `.claude/skills/fortress-repo/references/compiler.md:157`, "Traps of the compiled path", "Where an object overloads an inherited functional method by declarations of its own, and `self` is not the first parameter, the compiled dispatch method tests the receiver's type ... (ledger row 573) ... (ledger row 1038). Put `self` first in such overloads." is false now.
- FACTS: F-372's clause "but an object's dispatch method still tests the receiver in place of the argument, and where the receiver itself has the own declaration's parameter type, a call answers wrongly with no error ... (rows 1038 and 573)" is false now (record.md).

## Points to report

- The dispatch method as fixed: which local each type test and cast reads. Self first: the argument at place `j` in local `j`, unchanged (`DispatchSelfFirstProbe$C.pick?0`, identical bytecode). Self second: the argument before self in local 1 (`FunctionalMethodSelfSecondReceiverTested$Pq.mark?1`), and with three parameters the one after self in local 2 (`FunctionalMethodMeetNarrowedSelfNotFirst$C.pick?1`). Self last: the arguments at places 0 and 1 in locals 1 and 2 (`FunctionalMethodOverloadSelfLast$C.pick?2`, and the trait's springboard `$D$DefaultTraitMethods.pick?2`). The receiver is read from local 0 only as the arm's call target. Evidence: ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/OverloadSet.java:2504-2508, :1538, :1876, and the javap lines above. Reversible.
- The three expected failures promoted, each failing on the base and passing after: `FunctionalMethodOverloadSelfLast`, `FunctionalMethodCoverSelfSecond`, `FunctionalMethodSelfSecondReceiverTested` (renamed by `git mv` in c03be68be8; the runs `s35base` and `s35final` above). Reversible.
- Row 594's test after the fix: still failing, as before, with the same message: `XXXGenericFunctionalMethodSelfSecond` in the run `s35final`, 'Caused by: java.lang.NoSuchMethodError: 'java.lang.Object XXXGenericFunctionalMethodSelfSecond$Shape.\=tag?1??Arrow?...?(long, java.lang.String)'', then 'Saw expected failure (Exit code != 0)'. Its site is not the dispatch method. Reversible.
- The files edited, for STAGE_BLIND: section "The stages, and the files for STAGE_BLIND". Beyond the files the section names, one: `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/FunctionalMethodMeetNarrowedSelfNotFirst.fss`, row 571's test, gains `object N0o` and the case `pick(N0o, C, S1o)` (ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/FunctionalMethodMeetNarrowedSelfNotFirst.fss:8, :27). And `FunctionalMethodOverloadSelfLast.fss`, a promoted test, gains the trait case (ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/FunctionalMethodOverloadSelfLast.fss:19-23, :27-28). Reversible.

No step taken cannot be undone, and none acts against a decision on record.

## Decisions

1. **Where the local is computed: a method `argumentLocal(j, first)` in `OverloadSet`, overridden in `ForTraitOrObject`.** Ways not taken: an inline conditional at the two sites of `generateCall` (works, but states the layout twice in the base class, where `ForTraitOrObject` holds the layout's other facts, OverloadSet.java:2481-2493); `firstArg()` set to 1 for a functional method with the self place subtracted in `generateCall` (changes the varargs slots, OverloadSet.java:2031, and the generic arms' offset, :1523, which are right as they are); a static dispatch method with self in its place, as the top-level wrapper has (changes the method's descriptor and every interface that an object implements with it). Evidence: the javap of section "Each program run old against new". No decision on record names the mechanism; fork S1 gives the effect (CLIMB-BATCH-35.md:449).
2. **The inference branch's load (OverloadSet.java:1846) is left as it is.** It serves a generic arm converted to a function with self first, whose parameters are at their places; for a functional method no program reaches it (row 724 stops the code generator first). Way not taken: route it through `argumentLocal` too, which would be wrong for a converted arm and has no program to test it.
3. **Two cases added to existing tests rather than new files: the trait case in `FunctionalMethodOverloadSelfLast`, and self second of three in `FunctionalMethodMeetNarrowedSelfNotFirst`.** The skill adds a new case to the test that already asserts cases of its kind (tests-writing.md, "Names, comments, citations"). The trait case is placed before the object's so that its failure on the base shows (the object's case dies first otherwise). Ways not taken: new tests `FunctionalMethodTraitOverloadSelfLast` and `FunctionalMethodOverloadSelfMiddle`; no test of these shapes, which leaves the trait's springboard and an argument after self untested.
4. **The promoted programs keep their `REACHED` line**, as the precedent `NatRtTask` did (fd5cb48648, ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/NatRtTask.fss:22). Way not taken: removing it.
5. **No note on row 594.** Its line with the note "Not at row 573's site: with the dispatch method fixed (climb batch 35), the test dies with this message still." fails the notes limit: 'notes-length: 796 characters; at most 700' (`python3 explorations/coordinator/tools/ledger.py check --rows` on the row's line with the note), and the row's text stays true. Way not taken: a rewrite that cuts its notes; the fact is in this report and in record.md.

# Rung S (`rung-self-not-first-dispatch`): record lines for the gather

Climb batch 35, run 1, rung S. Branch `wip/rung-self-not-first-dispatch`, cut from 13f4fdea75; the fix is 9d9a67df82 on the branch (its hash as the gather lands it goes in the closes below). The detail is in `REPORT.md` beside this file.

## Findings

1. **The compiled dispatch method of a trait's or an object's functional method reads each argument at its own local, wherever self stands.** Holds on the compiled path, against the compiler's prelude, for declarations without static parameters of their own (a generic functional method overloaded beside a plain one stops the code generator first, row 724). The dispatch method is an instance method of the receiver's class: self in local 0, the other arguments after it in their order without self. `OverloadSet.argumentLocal` (ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/OverloadSet.java:2357-2363), overridden in `ForTraitOrObject` (OverloadSet.java:2495-2508), gives an argument before self's place the local after its place; the type test (:1538) and the arm's call (:1876) read it. Before, both read local `j` for the argument at place `j`, so with self second or last they read the receiver: a `ClassCastException` (row 573) or the object's own declaration for every argument (row 1038). Evidence: `ONE_JVM=1 explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-N/merged-tests/junit.sh s35final ProjectFortress/compiler_tests <the 46 *FunctionalMethod*.test files>` on 9d9a67df82, 'OK (64 tests)', the four tests below printing 'PASS'; on the base, 'ClassCastException: class FunctionalMethodOverloadSelfLast$C cannot be cast to class FunctionalMethodOverloadSelfLast$N1', '... FunctionalMethodCoverSelfSecond$Pq cannot be cast to class FunctionalMethodCoverSelfSecond$Ka', 'FAIL:  3 =/= 1; mark(1, Pq): only the inherited declaration applies, though the receiver is a K', '... FunctionalMethodMeetNarrowedSelfNotFirst$C cannot be cast to class FunctionalMethodMeetNarrowedSelfNotFirst$N0', and in a trait's springboard '... FunctionalMethodOverloadSelfLast$Do cannot be cast to class FunctionalMethodOverloadSelfLast$N1'. Tests: `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/FunctionalMethodOverloadSelfLast` (self last, an object and a trait), `FunctionalMethodCoverSelfSecond` (self second, a cover through `comprises`), `FunctionalMethodSelfSecondReceiverTested` (self second, the receiver of the parameter's type), `FunctionalMethodMeetNarrowedSelfNotFirst` (self second of three, an argument on each side). The dispatch method of a dotted method, of a top-level function and of a functional method with self first keeps its bytecode (javap of `DispatchSelfFirstProbe$C.pick?0`, old and new identical; REPORT.md, "Each program run old against new"). What it means: an object or trait may overload an inherited functional method with self anywhere; the skill's advice to put self first in such overloads is no longer needed.

2. **A call reaches an object's dispatch method of a functional method where the declaration that the top-level dispatch chooses has a more specific one below it in the object's overload set, as an inherited declaration does.** Measured in the programs of this rung. The top-level dispatch of the name, a static method over the declarations' wrappers with every argument at its own place, chooses by all the arguments; where the chosen declaration is the object's own and has none below it, its body is called at its exact signature (self last: `C`'s own `pick(n: N1, s: S0, self)` has `pick(n: N1, s: S1, self)` below it, so its signature holds a dispatch method; `FunctionalMethodMeetNarrowedSelfNotFirst$C`: the body at `pick?1(N1,S1)` beside the dispatch methods `pick?1(N0,S0)` and `pick?1(N0,S1)`, javap on the base). So `pick(n, C, S1o)` with `n: N0 = N1o` ran right on the base, and `pick(N0o, C, S1o)`, which runs `A`'s wrapper and lands on `C`'s dispatch method, died (REPORT.md, "The failing runs and the passing run"). What it means: a test of an object's dispatch method calls a declaration that has a more specific one below it in the object, with an argument that the more specific one does not take.

3. **Row 594's test still fails after the fix, with the same message:** `XXXGenericFunctionalMethodSelfSecond` in the run `s35final` on 9d9a67df82, 'Caused by: java.lang.NoSuchMethodError: 'java.lang.Object XXXGenericFunctionalMethodSelfSecond$Shape.\=tag?1??Arrow?fortress\|CompilerBuiltin\%Object,fortress\|AnyType\%Any?(long, java.lang.String)'', then 'Saw expected failure (Exit code != 0)'. Its site is not the dispatch method of an overload set: the method is not overloaded. What it means: row 594 stays open, at the site its notes name.

4. **`ProjectFortress/tests/disp2.fss` passes compiled on the base 13f4fdea75 and after the fix,** printing 'f PASS' and 'g PASS', where the baseline ladder records it at `run` with 'f FAIL' (explorations/compile-ladder/baseline-2026-09-19/ladder.tsv). It is not among the gate's 85 files (explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-34b/gate/ladder/ladder.tsv). Evidence: the ladder's subset driver (`explorations/compile-ladder/repair-r1-atomic-static/run-subset.sh`, copied into the rung's scratch as the skill's gate.md says) with the subset `tests disp2.fss` on 9d9a67df82, 'tests/disp2.fss crc=0 rrc=0', classified `pass`; on the old code, `old-fortress.sh /home/user/fortress-base42 <caches> compile disp2.fss` then `run disp2`, 'f PASS', 'g PASS'. What it means: an UP move since the baseline that predates this rung; the gate's list could take it.

## FACTS

A new entry under "Landed semantics":

- **The dispatch method of a trait's or an object's functional method reads each argument at its own local, wherever self stands.** The method is an instance method of the receiver's class, self in local 0 and the other arguments after it in their order; `OverloadSet.argumentLocal`, overridden in `ForTraitOrObject`, gives an argument before self's place the local after its place, for the type tests and the casts alike (rows 573 and 1038, fixed). A call reaches the method where the declaration that the top-level dispatch of the name chooses has a more specific one below it in the type, as an inherited one does; a declaration of the type with none below it is called at its exact signature, its body. Not reached: a generic functional method overloaded beside a plain one, on which the code generator stops first (row 724). Tests: `compiler_tests/FunctionalMethodOverloadSelfLast`, `FunctionalMethodCoverSelfSecond`, `FunctionalMethodSelfSecondReceiverTested`, `FunctionalMethodMeetNarrowedSelfNotFirst`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-self-not-first-dispatch/REPORT.md`, "What changed and why".

F-372 is false in its clause "but an object's dispatch method still tests the receiver in place of the argument, and where the receiver itself has the own declaration's parameter type, a call answers wrongly with no error: with `object Pq extends { K, P }` declaring `mark(x: K, self)` beside `P`'s `mark(x: Any, self)`, `mark(1, Pq)` gives 3 where walk gives 1 (rows 1038 and 573)". It now reads, from "so such a class loads": "so such a class loads, and its dispatch method reads each argument at its own local (rows 573 and 1038, fixed)." Evidence: `FunctionalMethodSelfSecondReceiverTested` passes on 9d9a67df82.

- **Row 1038**, closed by the fix: `ledger.py close 1038 --commit <the fix as landed; 9d9a67df82 on the branch> --test ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/FunctionalMethodSelfSecondReceiverTested.test`.
- **Row 594**: no change. Its line with the note "Not at row 573's site: with the dispatch method fixed (climb batch 35), the test dies with this message still." fails the notes limit, 'notes-length: 796 characters; at most 700' (`python3 explorations/coordinator/tools/ledger.py check --rows` on the row's line with the note), and the row's text stays true; finding 3 holds the fact.
- No new row.

The three `XXX` files that rows 573 and 1038 name (`XXXFunctionalMethodOverloadSelfLast`, `XXXFunctionalMethodCoverSelfSecond`, `XXXFunctionalMethodSelfSecondReceiverTested`) are renamed without the prefix by `git mv` in c03be68be8; the two closes above take the rows off the landing check's `xxx-gone` list.

## The skill, for the gather

`.claude/skills/fortress-repo/references/compiler.md:157` ("Traps of the compiled path": the compiled dispatch method tests the receiver's type where it should test the other argument's, rows 573 and 1038, "Put `self` first in such overloads.") is false after the change.

## Handover line

Climb batch 35, rung S (self not first): the dispatch method of a trait's or an object's functional method reads each argument at its own local (`OverloadSet.argumentLocal`, overridden in `ForTraitOrObject`), so rows 573 and 1038 close with their three tests promoted (`FunctionalMethodOverloadSelfLast`, with a trait case, `FunctionalMethodCoverSelfSecond`, `FunctionalMethodSelfSecondReceiverTested`) and a self-second-of-three case added to `FunctionalMethodMeetNarrowedSelfNotFirst`; the 46 functional method tests of the compiler track pass in one JVM; row 594's test still fails at its own site; no stage run, by the brief.

## Revival change

Revival change: none. The change brings the compiled path to what the specification says and walk does: a functional method's parameter type holds self at its place (`Specification/basic/overloading.tex:175-181`), and a call runs the most specific declaration applicable to it at run time (`Specification/basic/overloading.tex:298-312`); walk runs each of the four test programs to 'PASS' on the base. The team's code generator read the receiver for the argument before self, a defect, not a rule of the language.

# Rung R of climb batch 35: a numeral with a radix point keeps its leading zeros in its digit count, on both paths (row 960)

- problem: row 960, measured on the base under walk ('FAIL: a ZZ32: 2 =/= a ZZ32: 3') and compiled ('FAIL:  2 =/= 3') by the planner's probes, `explorations/compile-ladder/plan-35/probes/fixes-35.md:16`, `:38`
- spec: "the number $n$ of its digits, leading zeros among them", `Specification/basic/expressions/literals.tex:101`; the Working Draft's "let $n$ be the total number of digits", `Specification-1.0-frozen/basic/expressions/literals.tex:110`
- precedent: `ExprFactory.makeIntLiteralExpr(Span, String)`, which deletes apostrophes and U+202F and keeps every leading zero, `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/nodes_util/ExprFactory.java:609-632`
- deviation: none
- historical: `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/nodes_util/ExprFactory.java:1640-1643` (the team's lines, from their commit `0e5ed9a75c` of 2007-09-14, "Fixed handling leading zeroes in float literals."); `Specification/appendices/changes.tex:5486-5488` (a file of the 2012 tree; the clause removed is the revival's own text, `f36a651243`, `fcfd0aeb316`)

One launch worked this rung. Commits on `wip/rung-radix-point-leading-zeros`: `704d6fe747` (the tests and the fix), `535ad0a5c7` (Appendix I), and the commit of this report.

## What changed and why

`ExprFactory.makeFloatLiteralExpr(Span, String)` deleted every leading zero but one from the text that it keeps in the `FloatLiteralExpr` node (base `ExprFactory.java:1640-1643`), and `NumeralNumbers.of(FloatLiteralExpr)` counts the digit count `n` from that text on both paths (`nodes_util/NumeralNumbers.java:71-100`): the checker types the node from it (`scala_src/typechecker/impls/Misc.scala:474-477`; `CoercionOracle.scala:531-533` for a negated one), and walk binds a coercion's `n` from it (`interpreter/evaluator/values/Numerals.java:208-231`). So `00.5` was `RadixPointNumeral[\2, 1, 10, 5\]`, where P-174 and `literals.tex:101` make `n` 3. The edit deletes the four lines of the trim (fork R1): the node keeps the digits as written, apostrophes and narrow no-break spaces removed, its leading zeros among them, as an integer numeral's node already does. The values are unchanged: `intPart` is read by `new BigInteger(digits, base)`, which takes leading zeros, and `m` and `v` come from the digits after the point. Now at `ExprFactory.java:1637-1640`:

```java
        // Delete every apostrophe and U+202F NARROW NO-BREAK SPACE
        s = s.replace("'", "").replace(" ", "");

        int dotLoc = s.indexOf('.');
```

Tests: `ProjectFortress/tests/XXXRadixPointLeadingZerosWalk.fss` promoted by `git mv` to `RadixPointLeadingZerosWalk.fss` (component renamed), and its compiled twin `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/RadixPointLeadingZerosCompiled.fss` with `RadixPointLeadingZerosCompiledLink.test` (`link`) and `RadixPointLeadingZerosCompiled.test` (`link`, `run`, `run_out_contains=PASS`), from `explorations/compile-ladder/plan-35/probes/programs/compiler_tests/P35RadixPointLeadingZerosCompiled.fss` with its prefix dropped: a `value object Digits` whose coercion answers `bigToZZ64(n).asZZ32`, the helper bound as `FloatLiteralValuePrint.fss:17` binds it. It asserts 3 for `00.5` and 2 for `0.5`.

## The failing runs, on the base's code, before the edit was built

The worktree was seeded from the base build at `13f4fdea75` and held only the test files; the fix was edited and built after both runs.

## Every reader of the node's text, and what it now sees

Old against new, `bin/fortress compile` of a probe with `s: Small = 00.5` for a coercion `where { v < 3 }`: old 'The numeral 0.5 does not meet the where clause of the coercion to Small.', new 'The numeral 00.5 does not meet the where clause of the coercion to Small.' No test pins such a message with two leading zeros (the grep below).

Old against new, `bin/fortress compile` of `counted(00.5 MAX 0.1)` for the walk test's `Digits`: old '... not applicable to an argument of type RadixPointNumeral[\2,1,10,5\].', new '... RadixPointNumeral[\3,1,10,5\].'; walk refuses the call both times with the same 'Unification error: Closure/Constructor for counted param 1 (d:Digits) got arg 0.5:RR64 of type RR64'. A folded constant reaches no program's numeral coercion (P-174), and no library coercion reads `n` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:389`, `:635`; `LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss:68`; `CompilerBuiltin.fss:895`, `:957`), so only the message shows it. `00.5 + 0.0` folds through `written` to `(0.5)` and stays `[\2,1,10,5\]`, old and new. An integer operand kept so is rewritten to its value's digits (`:251-253`). A question for the curator, below.

## Where the fix belongs, and the precedent

The node is made once, by the parser's actions in `parser/Literal.rats:53-83` (`NumericLiteralExpr` and `NumericLiteralWithRadix`), which hands the numeral's whole text to `ExprFactory.makeFloatLiteralExpr` (`modules-and-phases.md` B.2; `compile-path-walkthrough.md`, section 1: the tree is the only form of the program, from the parser to the bytecode). The grammar already passes the digits as written; the factory dropped them. So the fix is in the factory, where both paths read it, and no phase after it can recover the zeros without the source.

The precedent is `makeIntLiteralExpr(Span, String)` in the same file (`ExprFactory.java:609-632`), which deletes apostrophes and U+202F and trims nothing. The file has no other site that trims a numeral's digits: `grep -n -i 'leading zero\|trim' nodes_util/ExprFactory.java` on the base printed only `:1640` and seven `Useful.immutableTrimmedList` calls, which trim lists of expressions. The trim came from the team's commit `0e5ed9a75c` (2007-09-14), which narrowed an earlier trim of every leading zero to all but one; nothing in the tree reads a text with one leading zero only.

## What the specification settles

`Specification/basic/expressions/literals.tex:100-101`: "The static arguments of a numeral type are the numeral's four numbers: the number $n$ of its digits, leading zeros among them;" and P-174 ("the digit count `n`"; its source `Specification-1.0-frozen/basic/expressions/literals.tex:110-111`, "let $n$ be the total number of digits"). The two tests' failing runs are the base's code, above.

## The finding

A numeral with a radix point now keeps its leading zeros in its digit count on both paths. Claim: `ExprFactory.makeFloatLiteralExpr(Span, String)` keeps the numeral's digits as written, apostrophes and U+202F removed, its leading zeros among them (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/nodes_util/ExprFactory.java:1637-1640`), as `makeIntLiteralExpr` does (`:609-632`); `NumeralNumbers.of(FloatLiteralExpr)` counts `n` from that text (`nodes_util/NumeralNumbers.java:78`), so `00.5` is `RadixPointNumeral[\3, 1, 10, 5\]` for the checker and for walk. Conditions: every numeral with a radix point that the parser makes; its value, `m` and `v` are unchanged (`x: RR64 = 00.5` prints '0.5' on both paths, old and new). Evidence: `ProjectFortress/tests/RadixPointLeadingZerosWalk.fss` failed on the base through `harness-one.sh`, 'FAIL: a ZZ32: 2 =/= a ZZ32: 3; literals.tex, section "Literals": 00.5 has three digits', and passes ('OK (1 test)'); `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/RadixPointLeadingZerosCompiled.test` failed on the base through `junit.sh`, 'FAIL:  2 =/= 3; ...', and passes ('OK (3 tests)', with its link test). `ant testSystem` (879 tests) and `ant testQuick` (1788, 86 and 263) pass on the fix's code; the count stage and the distance stage are the same as the last landed gate's, total 0 each. What it means: a program's own coercion over `RadixPointNumeral[\n, m, r, v\]` reads the digit count that P-174 and `Specification/basic/expressions/literals.tex:101` give. A checker message that quotes such a numeral shows it as written ('The numeral 00.5 does not meet the where clause of the coercion to Small.'), and a folded `MIN`, `MAX` or `|x|` that answers a written radix-point operand keeps its text, so its numeral type in a checker message counts the operand's zeros (`RadixPointNumeral[\3,1,10,5\]` for `00.5 MAX 0.1`); no program and no library coercion reads a folded constant's numbers (P-174; the curator's question in `REPORT.md`).

## FACTS.md

Under "Landed semantics", a new entry:

- **A numeral with a radix point keeps its digits as written in the node that both paths read, so its digit count `n` counts its leading zeros: `00.5` is `RadixPointNumeral[\3, 1, 10, 5\]`.** `ExprFactory.makeFloatLiteralExpr` removes only apostrophes and U+202F from the numeral's text (`nodes_util/ExprFactory.java:1637-1638`), as `makeIntLiteralExpr` does, and `NumeralNumbers.of` counts `n` from that text for the checker and for walk (`nodes_util/NumeralNumbers.java:71-100`); the value, `m` and `v` are read as before. A message that quotes the numeral shows it as written. Tests: `ProjectFortress/tests/RadixPointLeadingZerosWalk.fss`, `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/RadixPointLeadingZerosCompiled.test`. Detail: `explorations/compile-ladder/rung-radix-point-leading-zeros/REPORT.md`, "What changed and why" and "Every reader of the node's text, and what it now sees".

## The gap ledger

- **Row 960 closes**, after the fix lands: `ledger.py close 960 --commit <the landed commit of 704d6fe747> --test ProjectFortress/tests/RadixPointLeadingZerosWalk.fss --note "the compiled twin is ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/RadixPointLeadingZerosCompiled.test"`. ## Other entries that the change makes false

- POSITIONS.md, P-174's last sentence (`explorations/coordinator/POSITIONS.md:106`): "Rows 960 and 981 hold where the tree departs: the digit count of `00.5`, and walk running a numeral type written in a `comprises` clause." ## Revival change

**The change.** The team's parser kept a numeral with a radix point in its syntax tree with all but one of its leading zeros deleted from the numeral's text: `ExprFactory.makeFloatLiteralExpr` trimmed `00.5` to `0.5` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/nodes_util/ExprFactory.java:1640-1643` at `a874948ac`), while its integer numeral kept them (`makeIntLiteralExpr`, `:609-632`), so on both of the team's implementations the tree of `00.5` was that of `0.5`. result.ruling:
The blocking finding is upheld. Specification/appendices/changes.tex:6423-6425, written by the gather in O's commit d56eb8a882, says that the compiled checker refuses an override in a generic trait over any declaration that the trait inherits under a where clause. The code refuses less than that:
- OverloadingChecker.scala:384-385 extends the type analyzer with the trait's static parameters and None, so the where clause's bound is not held.
- :410-411 reads overriding pairs on that analyzer.
- STypesUtil.scala:1715-1716 pairs an override with an inherited declaration whose parameter types are equal to or below its own.
- :424 (checkOverridesSomething, :755-789) refuses only an override that is in no pair.
So an inherited declaration whose parameter types do not name the static parameter is read exactly. The reviewer's probe on e922c2ea1a confirms it: an override of g(x: Number) over g(x: ZZ32) typechecks, compiles and prints 'G', while an override of f(x: ZZ32) over f(x: T) is refused.

Right:
- The reviewer, on the overreach, on the clause being broader than row 1107's own claim, and on no gate being needed.
- Rung O's records (REPORT.md:84, :88, :134; row 1107), which name only the one form tested.

Wrong:
- The gather's RECORD.md:131, which says each clause 'states what the code does'.
- F-400, whose clause 'the checker refuses an override under a conditional extension that walk runs (row 1107)' overreaches the same way. The review did not name it.

Possibly still too broad: the reviewer's suggested wording. Per STypesUtil.scala:1716, an override whose parameter type is above the static parameter's declared bound, such as f(x: Any) over f(x: T), is paired even without the where clause holding, so the checker should accept it. I ran nothing. Repair step 1 settles the wording with one typecheck.
